# Plan: ClearPath-Comparable Precise Motion for BLDC

Status: researched plan for review, 2026-09-29. No implementation, firmware build, flashing, physical motion, or configuration changes performed. User supplied four architecture/gap documents and the 2026-08-29 motor/application XML backups, then was unavailable to clarify. Choices below are recommendations, not user-confirmed hardware facts.

## Recommendation and Scope

Add an opt-in, firmware-native `pm_interface` for encoder-based direct FOC. Deliver one precise axis first, keeping axis identity explicit so supported additional axes can be added later. Preserve existing BLDC/DC/FOC command behavior when PM is disabled. Separate a portable trajectory/state/controller core from firmware scheduling, encoder acquisition, transport, and board-specific I/O.

ClearPath-comparable means equivalent motion behaviors and observable results, not ClearCore API/ABI compatibility, MSP configuration compatibility, guaranteed ClearPath accuracy, safety certification, or electrical step/direction/HLFB compatibility. Use the ClearCore sources as behavioral references, not a wholesale SAM-specific code port. Retain native FOC current regulation, current/voltage/thermal protections, commutation and PWM.

First operational release: firmware C API, absolute/relative point-to-point moves, velocity/jog, explicit replacement, controlled stopping and abort/release, holding, bounded switch homing and reference setting, motion-specific protection/status, versioned UART/USB packet access where the board supports those transports. CAN forwarding follows the same protocol, not a real-time remote setpoint stream. Later stages cover presets/increments, following/current-limited torque behaviors, I/O adapters, diagnostics and local dual-axis common-start behavior. Coordinated contouring/distributed interpolation and jerk-limited S-curves are deferred.

## Evidence From Backups

Decode enums against this checkout, then confirm firmware version and live readback before commissioning. XML ConfigVersion=4 is not a board or firmware identity.

- motor_type=2 -> MOTOR_TYPE_FOC; foc_sensor_mode=2 -> FOC_SENSOR_MODE_HALL; m_sensor_port_mode=0 -> SENSOR_PORT_MODE_HALL. The backup does not enable a precision encoder. m_encoder_counts=8192 is a parameter, not proof of an installed encoder or its usable resolution.
- sp_pid_loop_rate=5 -> PID_RATE_1000_HZ, nominal RTOS position/speed PID rate. foc_f_zv=30000 is the saved PWM configuration, not a measured PID or sensor sampling frequency.
- si_motor_poles=14 and si_gear_ratio=1 are saved metadata requiring verification. p_pid_ang_div=1, p_pid_gain_dec_angle=0; the legacy position interface is angular.
- app_to_use=3 -> APP_UART, baud 115200; controller_id=102; CAN_BAUD_500K and CAN_MODE_VESC configured. Connector availability and actual host use are not established.
- timeout_msec=1000, timeout_brake_current=0; kill_sw_mode=DISABLED. The software timeout is active. This does not establish the existence or absence of external machine safety.
- s_pid_min_erpm=900, s_pid_allow_braking=0 and speed ramp=25000 ERPM/s are not appropriate assumptions for a low-speed bidirectional axis servo. PM gets its own validated control contract instead of silently changing these settings.
- l_current_max/min=+/-155.16 A, l_in_current_max=3 A, l_in_current_min=-200 A, configured voltage limits 12..72 V and regeneration cutoffs 1000/1100 V are commissioning review items, not hardware ratings. The supply's regeneration capability and physical current limits must be verified. Existing gains are not automatically suitable for the new servo.

## Verified Architecture to Reuse

- motor/mc_interface.c: per-motor state, mc_interface_select_motor_thread, motor selection, mc_interface_try_input, command setters, configuration and release/fault paths. Legacy setters return void; lock_override_once is a consumable permission bit, not an owner token. An ISR taking precedence in motor selection is not by itself proof of a selection race; the ISR clears its marker before returning.
- motor/mcpwm_foc.c: pid_thread around line 4484 runs position and speed PIDs in an RTOS thread with measured elapsed time; both local motors use motor 1's selected cadence. The feedback block near line 3866 and current loop operate separately. Add a PM branch at the existing outer-control scheduling point, not a competing application worker writing setpoints asynchronously.
- motor/foc_math.c: foc_run_pid_control_pos uses utils_angle_difference. Its non-indexed encoder branch can request 40 percent configured current. The speed PID has ramp/minimum-speed/braking semantics unsuitable for transparent precision reuse. Preserve these legacy paths; build an explicit unwrapped outer servo for PM.
- encoder/encoder.c: encoder_read_deg returns cached/driver-derived angle; encoder_index_found is not universal sensor health. encoder_read_deg_multiturn is a scaled legacy TS5700 path with a reset above abs(counter)=5000, not an unbounded raw-coordinate API. Add a non-destructive sensor snapshot contract for PM; do not infer sensor retention across power loss from this helper.
- timeout.c: the timeout worker releases/overrides locks, sends brake commands and feeds the independent MCU watchdog if monitored threads are healthy. PM must integrate this path explicitly and must not mask lost host ownership by internally resetting the timeout indefinitely.
- conf_custom.c has one custom configuration callback slot; commands.c has one custom application-data handler. Do not take these slots silently. conf_general's custom variable writer releases both motors and writes flash; PM persistence must not happen during active motion.
- Makefile: ALL_UNITTESTS currently contains utils_math. tests/utils_math/Makefile + make/unittest.mk provide native C with Google Test C++ wrappers. Add one pm_motion suite. Firmware build target is fw_<board>; vesc_tool container tasks are not BLDC firmware build tasks.

## Phase 0: Hardware and Acceptance Contract

1. Record board name/revision and build target, MCU flash/RAM budget, motor identification, verified pole pairs, mechanical transmission and load inertia, axis travel/speed/acceleration, required repeatability/absolute accuracy/following error and settle time. Select a supported encoder and board wiring; verify commutation/encoder pin conflicts, signal levels, sensor freshness/fault detection, maximum sample rate, and index/absolute reference behavior.
2. Define safe current/voltage/regeneration envelopes, a protected home/positive-limit/negative-limit input path and independent E-stop/energy removal. Vertical or hazardous loads require a validated holding-brake/safety design before powered testing. Do not use CAN/software stop as the only emergency protection or claim STO.
3. Adopt canonical signed 64-bit axis position ticks with a fixed documented per-axis ticks-per-unit scale and explicit unit identifier (rotary turns or linear units). Store large integer origins separately from bounded local fractional trajectory math. Define velocity and acceleration in axis units per second and per second squared, engineering-unit conversion in adapters, and explicit motor/load ratio/polarity. Do not reuse electrical RPM, p_pid_ang_div, or si_gear_ratio without validated conversion.
4. Precision readiness requires valid feedback and calibrated commutation. Referenced coordinates are additionally required for normal position/velocity commands with travel limits; only bounded homing/jog is allowed before referencing. Default power-on state is disabled and unreferenced. An absolute encoder may restore validity only after its retention and installation reference are independently qualified.

Gate: software work may proceed with a fake backend and synthetic encoder. Powered precision acceptance cannot proceed until the hardware/accuracy/stop-distance contract is completed; missing physical values are not filled with guessed defaults.

## Phase 1: API, Ownership and Portable State (Depends on Phase 0 Contract)

5. Define explicit axis ID, owner/session generation, command ID, typed configuration, capabilities, command acceptance/rejection, durable terminal result and coherent status snapshot. Commands: configure, enable, disable, set-reference, home, move-absolute, move-relative, velocity/jog, replace, stop-decelerated, abort-release, clear-fault, query-status and renew-owner-lease. No heap allocation or unbounded queues in the motion path.
6. Use one active request per axis for the first release. Default submissions return BUSY while active; explicit replacement is allowed for supported move classes only. Relative position moves use the previous commanded endpoint, matching ClearCore; while replacing an active positional move, the base is the superseded endpoint. A velocity or homing request has no positional endpoint, so relative replacement is rejected. Rejected replacements leave the old move unchanged. No hidden FIFO.
7. Separate lifecycle (disabled/unreferenced/ready/homing/moving/settling/holding/stopping/faulted) from trajectory phase and terminal result. Completion is endpoint generation finished AND fresh measured position within tolerance AND measured velocity below threshold for a continuous configured settle duration. Include settle timeout, following-error faults, cancelled/superseded outcomes and exactly one terminal outcome per command. Holding remains under the owner after completion; losing tolerance is observable and never restarts the completed request.
8. Centralize state mutation in the PM outer-control tick. Thread-side commands enter bounded mailboxes and return accepted/pending or a rejection; the status distinguishes submitted, active and terminal. Acceptance reserves ownership and capacity, activation rechecks safety/config epoch, and immediate faults can still terminate an accepted request before activation. Publish multibyte state with bounded critical sections/double buffering; do not rely on volatile or allow ISR readers to spin on preempted writers.
9. Enforce ownership per motor in mc_interface. Ordinary commands cannot take over while PM owns the axis; release/fault/kill/shutdown paths can always revoke authority. Use a private, explicit-axis backend entry with an owner/generation check, not lock_override_once every tick. Tool detection, application stop, encoder reset and configuration changes must quiesce/revoke PM before accessing the drive. Configuration/reference/scaling changes require disabled motion; forced legacy changes abort PM first and increment the generation so old mailboxes cannot restart it.

Gate: native state tests prove acceptance, BUSY/replacement semantics, stale owner rejection, cancellation, double-submit behavior, reference lifecycle and exactly-once terminal results before integration.

## Phase 2A: Deterministic Profiles (Depends on Phase 1; Parallel With 2B)

10. Implement host-testable C trapezoidal/triangular point-to-point profiles with separate acceleration/deceleration bounds and signed endpoints. Support zero/short moves, either direction, nonzero initial velocity, speed reduction, reverse direction after braking and velocity ramp-to-zero. Explicit retarget starts from the current commanded position and velocity, never resetting to measured position and introducing a discontinuity.
11. Keep commanded position/velocity continuous; acceleration steps are allowed for the first-release trapezoidal profile. Calculate stopping distance and feasible overshoot for moving initial conditions. A target behind the current stopping point is handled with a bounded stop/reversal only if its full excursion is legal; otherwise reject replacement or fault a now-infeasible stop. End-point-only soft-limit checking is insufficient. Reject nonfinite/invalid values and overflow before reserving a command.
12. Advance with the same accepted elapsed dt as the outer servo. Account for bounded normal jitter and clamp integration to exact terminal targets; large/invalid dt triggers a scheduler fault rather than a giant catch-up setpoint. The fast tick performs bounded work only. Start nominally at the saved 1 kHz outer-loop rate, but characterize achievable cadence and CPU load before claiming any timing guarantee.

Gate: analytic and generated tests for distances, endpoint accuracy in ticks, velocity/acceleration limits, braking envelopes, reversal, retarget continuity, jitter and numeric boundaries. Profiles reaching the endpoint are not themselves move completion.

## Phase 2B: Encoder/Axis Feedback (Depends on Phase 1; Parallel With 2A)

13. Add a coherent PM snapshot carrying source/motor identity, position sample, acquisition timestamp/sequence, health/index/commutation validity and reset epoch. Timestamp fresh sensor acquisition, not every reread of a stale cached value. Support a qualified initial encoder; add only the driver hooks it needs and report unsupported modes clearly.
14. Unwrap single-turn samples into signed integer turns/ticks with bounded modulo differences and physically possible velocity/time checks. Enforce less than half-turn ambiguity per fresh sample and reject long gaps, impossible jumps and wrap/reset anomalies. Retain fractional remainder rather than rounding away small increments. A valid stationary value is not sensor loss; timestamp or driver health is required to distinguish a stalled data stream.
15. Maintain reference offset separately from raw accumulation and apply direction, sensor inversion, motor/load scaling and any commutation conversion exactly once. Reboot, encoder reset, invalid feedback or relevant reconfiguration invalidates reference. An ordinary motion cancellation need not invalidate a still-observed reference, but must not preserve it without continuous valid tracking. Do not persist inferred turns as an absolute power-loss reference.
16. If supporting TS multi-turn later, expose raw count/angle/health without the existing scaled getter's auto-reset side effect. Treat rollover/retention as sensor-specific capabilities. Existing global encoder configuration does not establish two independent precision sources; reject duplicate sensor binding on dual-motor boards unless explicitly supported.

Gate: synthetic traces cover 359->0 and 0->359, many turns, both polarity settings, geared axes, stationary data, startup without index, stale packets, sensor reset, quantization, overflow and wrong-axis identity.

## Phase 3: Native FOC Servo Integration (Depends on 1, 2A and 2B)

17. Add a dedicated PM backend mode by appending rather than renumbering existing control-mode values. In pid_thread, run PM outer control for an owned motor instead of legacy position/speed PID; legacy calls remain intact for unowned motors. Use the existing timing source with explicit nominal cadence and measured-dt bounds; ensure shutdown/reinitialization cannot leave the PM tick alive after backend teardown. Allocate initialized PM state before enabling hooks; do not enable motion at boot.
18. Implement unwrapped position error -> bounded velocity demand with trajectory velocity feed-forward -> encoder-velocity feedback/current demand. Make gains PM-specific, with explicit units, anti-windup, filtered measured velocity and bumpless state initialization. Feed signed iq demand through the native FOC current-control path and its existing dynamic current, bus-current, voltage and thermal restrictions. Apply a separate conservative PM current/torque cap; record saturation and stop claiming profile tracking when following error exceeds bounds. Physical torque units require calibrated torque constant; otherwise expose current and explicitly estimated torque only.
19. Do not feed normalized PM positions through mc_interface_set_pid_pos or inherit its 40-percent index search. Do not repurpose s_pid_min_erpm or globally disable speed ramps/braking checks. PM owns its low-speed bidirectional servo and optional referencing sequence. Ensure zero-demand enabled hold is distinct from release: audit current-off threshold, PWM-on/idle handling, state transitions, field weakening and all control-mode tests for the new mode.
20. Bound the feedback publication work in the ISR; profile calculation, controller update and lifecycle belong in the existing outer thread. Add an ISR/backend checked output-validity deadline and owner epoch so a stalled PM tick cannot leave stale iq applying indefinitely. Respect immediate electrical faults independent of thread timing. Measure cycle budget, dt distribution and snapshot critical-section latency on the actual target; reserve deadline failure margins and report overruns.

Gate: fake-backend integration shows +/-multiple revolutions, large following error without shortest-path reversal, correct polarity, zero-speed hold, bounded current, saturation recovery, disabled/faulted no-output, stalled-tick fail-safe, and no competing controller writes. No-load HIL then validates polarity/feedback at restricted energy before longer moves.

## Phase 4: Protection, Stop and Homing (Depends on 3; State Tests Start in Phase 1)

21. Integrate fault, release, timeout, application lifecycle, flash/config save and shutdown so they revoke PM authority before later setpoints can run. Existing electrical shutdown remains authoritative. Latch a separate PM fault/result even when the legacy electrical fault timer clears after its configured interval. Clearing requires cleared inputs, a valid sensor and explicit acknowledgement; enabling and submitting a new command are separate actions. Never resume the previous command automatically.
22. Keep owner heartbeat separate from planner activity and unrelated COMM_ALIVE/legacy traffic. Default to the saved 1000 ms external lease until machine qualification selects a value; refresh only for validated owner traffic. First-release communications loss defaults to the existing release-style behavior. Optional controlled-stop-on-link-loss requires configured deceleration, valid feedback, a bounded stop deadline and explicit arbitration with timeout.c so its brake writes cannot compete. Kill input/electrical fault/hardware E-stop are never delayed by this optional policy. Preserve independent MCU watchdog monitoring and add PM-tick monitoring.
23. Define stop-decelerated (ramp velocity to zero, then hold or release as requested), disable/abort-release (remove commanded torque, no stopping-distance guarantee), and fault shutdown distinctly. Directional travel limits reject inward commands and initiate the qualified stop; permitted escape requires explicit fault acknowledgement and limited recovery/jog authority, not automatic reversal. Soft limits include braking margin and enforce a valid reference. Impossible stopping distance escalates to the qualified machine response and a latched fault.
24. Provide board-neutral timestamped home/limit/stop inputs with polarity/debounce/freshness; adapters own GPIO/remote wiring. Implement switch homing: handle initially active switch, bounded backoff, fast seek, controlled stop, backoff, slow re-approach, latch, reference assignment and optional final offset move. Every state has maximum time/travel/current and abort behavior. Separate mechanical homing from encoder/commutation alignment. Permit bounded index acquisition only through an explicit procedure; never silently use the legacy torque search. Sensor stuck on/off, contradictory limits and stale remote inputs fault deterministically.
25. Hard-stop/current-detected homing is a later opt-in mode requiring a mechanically qualified hard stop, reduced torque, speed, timeout/travel bounds and repeated confirmation. A current threshold alone is not a certified collision detector. Physical input E-stop status supplements but never replaces independent safety wiring.

Gate: injected faults at every lifecycle/profile/homing phase, limit escape tests, loss of comms/feedback, forced reconfigure/release/save, unindexed startup, input chatter/stuck inputs, repeated clear/enable, and power-cycle behavior. HIL verifies measured stopping distance, home repeatability and no spontaneous restart.

## Phase 5: Configuration and Protocol (Depends on 1 and 4; Codec Tests Can Run Earlier)

26. Keep PM configuration separate from existing mc_configuration/app_configuration schemas in the first release, avoiding generator/signature churn and preserving the supplied backups. Use versioned length/CRC records with disabled defaults and range checks. Add a dedicated reserved PM EEPROM-emulation address region after checking page/virtual-table capacity against every enabled build; do not use unreserved HW/custom variable addresses. Two generation-tagged records with commit-last and CRC protect against interrupted saves; invalid/missing data boots disabled. Store only disabled, after all local motors are quiescent because flash writes and existing storage helpers affect both motors. Do not save live moves, owner leases or a presumed valid multi-turn coordinate.
27. Add one dedicated appended COMM_PACKET_ID for a versioned PM envelope and subcommands; do not reuse/reinterpret COMM_SET_POS or overwrite the sole custom-data handler. Validate payload length, schema version, axis, command ID, owner generation, numeric bounds and lease before parsing/applying. Reply via the current request's reply_func, avoiding mutable global routing for delayed responses. ACK means accepted/pending, not physically complete; poll status for active/terminal result. Duplicate (session, command ID) requests must not execute a relative move twice; use bounded monotonic/idempotence rules and distinguish retransmit from altered-payload collision.
28. Reuse existing packet framing/buffer helpers and UART/USB dispatch; retain APP_UART, node ID and baud from the user's backup unless they explicitly reconfigure later. PM-specific status returns configured capabilities, source validity, reference, requested/commanded/measured position and velocity, state/result, fault cause, active limits, estimated torque/current, saturation and timestamps. Add CAN forwarding of the same finite requests after a transport test; no CAN clock synchronization or shared trajectory is implied. Bound reply sizes and status rate for 115200 baud/500 kbit CAN.
29. Keep UI work and other repositories outside the initial implementation. Use in-firmware C tests and terminal diagnostics for first bring-up; document packet layouts sufficiently for a host implementation. A subsequent VESC Tool project can add import/export, parameter editing, trajectory plots and commissioning workflow. Do not commandeer conf_custom's single callback slot to avoid coordinated tool work.

Gate: codec round-trip, malformed/truncated/oversized packet tests, signed 64-bit positions, duplicate relative commands, stale generations/reconnect, owner loss, multi-client reply routing, UART/CAN loss/reordering, old command/config compatibility and interrupted persistence tests.

## Phase 6: Broader ClearPath Behavior Roadmap (Depends on Qualified Core)

30. Maintain a traceability table for all 20 examples in documentation/clearpath_examples_behavior_map.md, linking each comparable behavior to PM API, tests and hardware prerequisites. Software presets substitute for MSP tables; physical voltage-level timing remains in adapters. Never report all-example parity based only on a generic Move command.
31. First-release mappings: MovePositionAbsolute/Relative -> position profiles; MoveVelocity -> velocity control; MotorStatusRegister -> status/latched diagnostics; switch-based referencing covers home-dependent positioning with different homing semantics explicitly documented. UserSeeksHome's hard-stop behavior remains dependent on the later qualified hard-stop mode.
32. Next: Abs2/4/16 preset positions, Move2/4 increments and pulse-burst count semantics using named stored parameters and validated selector/trigger events. MC examples requiring hard-stop homing depend on step 25; home-switch variants use step 24. Enable remains an authorization operation: map increment triggers to explicit events, not a dangerous electrical enable toggle.
33. Add selected/ramped velocity and ManualVelocity delta requests; continuous following position and signed velocity with filtering, slew limits, deadband and command freshness; command lock freezes target under a documented hold policy. Add bounded current/estimated-torque commands and velocity with variable current/torque limit. Torque mode requires independent overspeed/travel protection; a current cap alone cannot stop an externally driven load. Physical analog/PWM/quadrature/trigger decoding is optional and only on qualified pins/I/O hardware, not silently enabled from the existing servo_out setting.
34. ASG-with-measured-torque and SpeedOutput map to software status with documented units and estimation accuracy; emitting physical HLFB requires an external adapter, so no electrical HLFB equivalence is claimed. Follow/torque/preset modes call the common lifecycle/protection core, not parallel bespoke motor setters.
35. DualAxisSynchronized comes last: two verified independent feedback sources and power stages, atomic group acceptance/arming, a shared local start epoch and dt, per-axis profiles, completion only when both settle, and common fault/stop policy. Verify sensor sharing and motor-1 cadence coupling first. This provides the example's common-start/common-fault behavior, not path contouring. Multi-VESC synchronized motion requires a separate timestamp/clock/safety design and is deferred.

Gate: every mapped behavior has deterministic core/adapter tests, bounded failure states and the applicable HIL acceptance trace; unsupported electrical interfaces/capabilities return explicit unsupported status.

## Verification and Rollout

- In the user's persistent WSL shell, prerequisites are native GCC/G++, make and configured Google Test for host tests, and the repo's ARM toolchain for firmware. Do not use the unrelated VESC Tool Docker tasks or assume PlatformIO applies to this Makefile project.
- Register pm_motion, then run `make ut_pm_motion_run` after each small motion slice. Use `make ut_utils_math_run` for existing utility regression and `make all_ut_run` for the integrated registered suite. Add sanitizer execution where supported and size/overflow assertions for 64-bit serialization/local float precision. These tests have not been run during planning.
- Build `make fw_<confirmed-board>` with PM disabled and enabled, and one supported dual-motor compile target when introducing shared paths; placeholders are intentionally unresolved until hardware identification. Check flash/RAM/map growth, stack use and no new warnings. No firmware flashing until physical gates pass.
- Fake backend tests exercise shared control ownership, command/fault interleavings, persistent record failures, sensor traces, malformed/replayed protocol packets and every homing state. Regression tests establish old angular setpoints, speed/current modes and old XML/config packet round trips remain unchanged with PM off.
- HIL staged sequence: power stage disabled -> read encoder while turning shaft manually -> guarded no-load low-current polarity tests -> bounded slow moves -> reference/homing and both limits -> repeated loaded moves and thermal/regeneration tests. Capture encoder position, reference, velocity, iq/current limits, bus voltage, command/result IDs, error, sensor age, tick jitter and faults. Compare load-side position with an independent reference when accuracy is claimed.
- Numerical pass criteria are the Phase 0 machine requirements; exact endpoint generation is necessary but insufficient. Measure bidirectional repeatability, reversal/backlash error, speed and acceleration, settle duration, max following error, stop distances, home repeatability and performance at thermal/current limits. Do not assert ClearPath-equivalent accuracy or industrial safety from a compile or host unit tests.
- Inject UART/CAN disconnects, unrelated keepalives, duplicate commands, E-stop/limit transitions, encoder unplug/reset, scheduler overruns and electrical faults. Verify no stale request restarts after clearing/reconnecting or flash/config updates. Validate hardware safety independently of firmware status.
- Deploy opt-in with conservative qualified limits and saved original firmware/backups. Build and test before write/flash; never automatically restore the supplied high-current/regen parameters for commissioning. Rollback disables PM and restores legacy firmware/config only through the normal authorized procedure.

## Explicit Boundaries and Deferred Choices

- User-confirmed only: wants a plan to add ClearPath-comparable motion to BLDC and supplied these backups. Direct FOC/single-axis-first/full staged roadmap/C API plus UART are recommended assumptions because the user was unavailable.
- Exact board, encoder, mechanics, units scale, accuracy numbers, allowed stopping response and safety wiring remain commissioning inputs, not obstacles to host-side implementation and not permission for physical motion.
- Initial precision capability is encoder-qualified FOC only. Sensorless/Hall precision fallback, BLDC/DC precision servo, generalized multi-encoder infrastructure, automatic sensorless recovery, step/direction electrical compatibility, external ClearPath drive control, hard-stop homing by default, jerk-limited profiles, arbitrary command queues, path contouring, distributed clock synchronization, permanent position retention and safety certification are excluded.
- Preserve existing XML files and legacy schemas. Protocol and PM storage are versioned independently; VESC Tool UI/schema integration and protected external I/O adapters are later scoped work.
